body.en: A and B are mutually exclusive if $A \cap B = \varnothing$: they cannot happen together. Events $E_1, \dots, E_n$ are exhaustive if $E_1 \cup \dots \cup E_n = S$: at least one must happen. If they are pairwise mutually exclusive and also exhaustive, they split S into separate parts. The simple events of S are always mutually *exclusive and exhaustive*.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A die is rolled. A: even number, B: odd number, C: number is less than or equal to 3. Find A intersection C, A union C and B - C, and decide whether A and B are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
A intersection C = {2}; A union C = {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}; B - C = {5}.
A intersection B equals the empty set and A union B equals S.
So the answer is A and B are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
